Chandra Finds Possible Origin of ‘Treble Clef’ Waves

gist: Astronomers used NASA’s Chandra observatory to explain the Treble Clef radio wave formation.
The structure was likely caused by a black hole outburst and galaxy cluster collision.
Researchers published their findings in the Astronomy & Astrophysics journal on Wednesday.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Astronomers used NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory and other telescopes to investigate a radio wave formation nicknamed the Treble Clef, hidden behind the Milky Way. They determined it is hosted by two merging galaxy clusters and likely formed in a two-stage process involving a supermassive black hole outburst followed by a cluster collision.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The discovery explains a formation that was previously difficult to understand because intervening stars, gas, and dust from the Milky Way block the view from Earth, revealing how black hole outbursts and cluster collisions interact.
